title: Joining text: &, CONCAT and TEXTJOIN
explanation: Last lessons you split text apart. Now the opposite: a mailing list stores first name, last name, city and state in separate columns, and you need to **join** them into full names, locations and email addresses.

tasks.prompt: In F2, join Maya's first and last name with a space between: =A2 & " " & B2.
tasks.teach: The **&** sign joins text together. Excel adds nothing between the pieces, so you add the space yourself, as text in quotes: `" "`.
hints: Join A2, then a space in quotes, then B2.

tasks.prompt: In G2, make the location in the style "Boston, MA": the city, a comma and a space, then the state.
hints: The bit in the middle is ", " (a comma and a space, in quotes).

tasks.prompt: In H2, build Maya's email: first.last@wes.edu, all lowercase. Wrap the joined text in LOWER: =LOWER(A2 & "." & B2 & "@wes.edu").
tasks.teach: You can put a whole join inside another function. Here LOWER makes the finished email lowercase.
hints: Join first name, ".", last name and "@wes.edu", all inside LOWER( ).

tasks.prompt: In I2, join all 4 columns with a comma and space between each, using TEXTJOIN: =TEXTJOIN(", ", TRUE, A2:D2).
tasks.teach: **TEXTJOIN(separator, ignore_empty, range)** joins a whole range at once, putting the separator between each piece. TRUE means skip empty cells. It's much shorter than lots of & signs.
hints: The separator is ", ", then TRUE, then the range A2:D2.

tasks.prompt: Last one: copy F2:I2 down to row 6, so everyone has a full name, location, email and summary.
hints: Select F2:I2, copy, select F3:I6, paste.

recap: The & sign joins text, and you add spaces or commas yourself in quotes. TEXTJOIN joins a whole range with a separator. Wrap a join in LOWER or PROPER to fix its capitals.
